name: Ukraine

advisory.note: Ukraine is at war. Governments across Europe advise against all travel to the country, and this page exists as a record of a place rather than as an invitation to visit it. Nothing here should be read as a suggestion that leisure travel is currently appropriate.

tagline: The largest country wholly within Europe, with the mother of Slavic cities on the Dnipro.
summary: Ukraine holds Europe's richest farmland, a Black Sea coast, the Carpathian foothills, and in Kyiv one of the oldest continuously important cities in the Slavic world — the monastery caves there date from 1051. Lviv's centre is Habsburg and intact. This page records what the country is; when travel is possible again, it will be updated by people who have been.

season.note: Historically, late spring and early autumn. This is context, not a recommendation — see the advisory above.

getting_around: Historically an extensive railway network with overnight sleepers between all major cities. Current conditions are governed by wartime restrictions, curfews and air-raid procedures.
food: Borscht, which is on the UNESCO intangible heritage list as Ukrainian
Varenyky, filled dumplings, sweet or savoury
Salo, cured pork fat, taken far more seriously than outsiders expect

festivals.name: Ivana Kupala, midsummer fire and water rites

know: Check your own government's current travel advice; at the time of writing it advises against all travel.
This country is excluded from the Journey Planner for that reason.
Support for Ukrainian cultural institutions is possible from outside without travelling.

regions.name: Kyiv & the Centre
regions.summary: The capital on the Dnipro, its monastery caves and its golden domes.

cities.name: Kyiv
cities.summary: A city founded in the 5th century on hills above a wide river, with a cave monastery from 1051 beneath it.
highlights: The Lavra caves, and the monks buried in them
Andriivskyi descent, the old artists' street
The deepest metro station in the world at Arsenalna, 105 metres down

regions.name: Western Ukraine
regions.summary: Habsburg Lviv and the Carpathian foothills beyond it.

cities.name: Lviv
cities.summary: An Austro-Hungarian city with an intact centre on the UNESCO list, a coffee tradition and a chocolate one.
highlights: Rynok square and the merchant houses around it
The Lychakiv cemetery, a park of 19th-century sculpture
Coffee houses that predate most of Vienna's
